newsitem.title: UK: NWE low sulphur fuel weak on supply, Italy data.
newsitem.headline: NWE low sulphur fuel weak on supply, Italy data.

text.p: NWE low sulphur fuel oil markets were weaker on Thursday amid continued good supply and bearish data from Italian Industry, traders said.

Low sulphur cargo offers were heard at $110 cif Italy for arrival in early March. More avails loom from across the Atlantic and shipbrokers thought as much as 400,000 tonnes of high and low sulphur fuel would load mid-month to sail to Europe from across the Atlantic.

Fresh data from Italian trade group Unione Petrolifera showed Italy's power sector consumed 33 percent less low sulphur fuel oil in January than last year. Traders saw this as particularly bearish, given that Italian electricity consumption last month was only 1.2 percent lower than in January last year, according to data from ENEL.
Growing natural gas supplies account for the bulk of the difference, analysts said.
Offers in NWE were plentiful, and no business was heard since traders bought two U.K.-origin cargoes on Tuesday: one at around the quoted fob NWE high and the other at around the quoted cif Med low.
High sulphur fuel oil was flat. Barges traded at $97 fob NWE in the morning and offers were later pegged at around $97.
High sulphur cargoes were quiet and dealers assessed prices at around $92/$95 cif NWE.
